title: Choose the bench structure
question: The roll assigned Same-frame inventory. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Same-frame inventory
options.thesis: The bench rests as a compact inventory; opening a tool deploys it in the same frame.
options.viewport: A compact inventory of the seven tools fills the shell; choosing one deploys that tool's existing interior into the same stage, with collapse returning to inventory.
options.risk: The inventory rest can read as a home page if collapse is not instant.

raised.raise: Compact rest deploys one tool into the same field; collapse returns.
Chrome never restyles; only the working cell changes.
Copy is the one obvious commit; tools group by job.

options.label: Clustered rail
options.thesis: Related converters sit as families in a persistent rail; one tool occupies the stage.
options.viewport: A left rail clustered into Type, Assets, and Text; the current tool's existing interior fills the stage without restyling the frame.
options.risk: Clustering can hide a tool you reach for by name.

options.label: Instrument strip
options.thesis: Tools are a horizontal instrument bar; the stage below never becomes a different place.
options.viewport: Identity and all seven tools share one top strip; the tool interior fills the remaining canvas as a single stage.
options.risk: A growing set overflows a horizontal strip faster than a rail.

options.label: Desk instrument
options.thesis: Tools are grouped keys on one chassis; the current tool is the display.
options.viewport: A grouped key strip switches tools; the existing tool interior fills the display; copy sits as the one commit control.
options.case: Wins on audience identification as a desk bench; loses on clarity because these tools are full forms, not single keys.
options.risk: A key-grid can fight the full-form interiors we must keep.

options.label: Full-viewport snap
options.thesis: One tool owns the whole viewport; the next is one snap away.
options.viewport: A single tool fills the frame; flicking snaps to the next complete tool.
options.case: Fuses poorly: you do not browse converters by flicking.
options.kept: Once open, the current tool owns the stage.
options.risk: Turns a named lookup into a feed.

options.label: Live board
options.thesis: Chrome columns never move; only the working row updates.
options.viewport: A ruled board of tools; switching flaps the content cell, not the page.
options.case: The unmoving grid is useful; the concourse metaphor is not this user's scene.
options.kept: Chrome never restyles when the working cell changes.
options.risk: Reads as a departure board, not a workbench.

options.label: Card stack
options.thesis: Each tool is an addressable card; back retraces the exact trail.
options.viewport: Seven linked cards with hash addresses; back walks the trail.
options.case: Loses on clarity: a stack of cards is the seven-pages problem.
options.kept: Hash URLs stay addressable; back retraces exactly.
options.risk: Preserves the fragmentation this brief is here to kill.

options.label: Deployable sheet
options.thesis: A compact packet deploys one cell into a working field.
options.viewport: Inventory as a compact packet; opening a tool deploys that cell across the stage.
options.case: The deploy/collapse mechanic is the raise; the origami world is not this bench.
options.kept: Compact rest deploys one tool; collapse returns.
options.risk: The fold reads as spectacle on a CSS utility bench.

options.label: Depth axis
options.thesis: You descend from inventory into a tool as depth.
options.viewport: A vertical dive from overview into a tool, with an explicit turnaround back.
options.case: Descending is navigation into a destination, which fights one bench.
options.kept: Collapse back to inventory is a first-class control, not browser back.
options.risk: Makes switching tools feel like leaving the surface.
